# Selene privacy and outbound-data audit

Audit date: 2026-09-13. Baseline commit: `403ad0a562bbc86ff5a0e26c23544dbd99235c15`.

## Result

The baseline contained automatic usage reporting to the original maintainer's server, remote dashboard content and scripts, an automatic package-version check, and an optional token counter that submitted tool text to an AI API. Those paths have been removed. Additional telemetry in optional agent and language-server dependencies has been disabled as described below. Bundled agent instructions explicitly prohibit sending project data to external recipients unless the user requests it.

This is a source and behavior audit of this checkout, with a complete file inventory and targeted dependency review. It is **not a guarantee that arbitrary language servers, installers, project commands, plugins, or future dependency versions cannot communicate externally**. Selene runs these programs with the user's operating-system permissions. The remaining network paths and limits are part of this report, not exceptions hidden behind a “telemetry-free” claim.

## Scope and method

The review covers first-party runtime Python, all language-server adapters and their static configuration, prompts, contexts, modes, hooks, project memories, frontend HTML/CSS/JavaScript, scripts, CI, packaging, containers, Nix configuration, docs, and test fixtures. The original checkout contained 1,065 tracked files. Names in this report use the new project name, including when discussing baseline locations.

The reproducible inventory in [security/repository-inventory.json](security/repository-inventory.json) lists every current non-generated repository file, its SHA-256, category, URL domains, suspicious instruction/transfer/telemetry signals, and candidate Python network/process/deserialization calls. The reports themselves, Git history, ignored virtual environments, caches, and generated documentation are excluded from this inventory. Binary artwork is inventoried as bytes rather than claimed to have been source-reviewed.

[security/dependency-inventory.json](security/dependency-inventory.json) records the installed, locked Python environment, including development and optional AI extras: distribution versions, fingerprints, and candidate signals across Python, JavaScript, and PTH files. Compiled extensions, wheels for other platforms, and arbitrary remote language-server installations are outside that text scan. Dependency signals were traced selectively to actual sends and their callers; comments, documentation URLs, local logging, and LSP `telemetry/event` messages were not automatically classified as Internet telemetry.

[security/language-server-inventory.md](security/language-server-inventory.md) enumerates every adapter resource and its download/process-related signals. Runtime sinks, credential propagation, prompts that could request disclosure, URLs assembled from configuration, browser resource loading, package-manager commands, and persistence were reviewed together. A static keyword scan alone is not the basis for the findings below.

## Findings and changes

| ID | Finding in the baseline | Data / destination / trigger | Change and current behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F01 | Automatic startup usage beacon | On agent startup, GET to `oraios-software.de`; query fields included OS, version, language backend, context, and dashboard status. The host also receives ordinary connection metadata. No source-code field was present in this request. | Removed the call, implementation, and reporting import from `src/selene/agent.py`. There is no opt-in path left for this beacon. |
| F02 | Remote news and promotional dashboard content | Server retrieved news JSON with ETags; the browser fetched a banner manifest, followed remote image URLs, and inserted remote news HTML. These contacted the same maintainer host. Remote HTML was also an injection and future exfiltration surface. | Removed news polling, cache, routes, banner rotation, UI, remote HTML rendering, news data, and the SSH/SCP publishing script. |
| F03 | Dashboard update check | Background GET to PyPI on dashboard startup exposed IP/time/version-interest metadata. | Removed the check and associated API/UI fields and helper module. |
| F04 | Remote executable browser assets | Google Fonts and unpinned Chart.js/plugin CDN scripts loaded whenever the dashboard opened. Scripts could read the dashboard's logs and project details. Generated docs also used a MathJax CDN. | Bundled fixed Chart.js 4.5.1, datalabels 2.2.0, and MathJax 3.2.2 with licenses. Removed remote fonts. Dashboard CSP allows resources and connections only from its own origin; it also sets no-referrer, no-store, nosniff and framing restrictions. |
| F05 | API-based token estimation | The optional Anthropic estimator sent complete tool inputs/results to the token-count API just to produce usage statistics. | Removed the estimator and enum option. Default character counting is fully local. Existing configurations selecting the removed API counter must switch to `CHAR_COUNT` or `TIKTOKEN_GPT4O`. Optional tiktoken counting downloads vocabulary files if uncached, but never sends the counted text. Anthropic is now an optional agent-integration dependency. |
| F06 | Optional Agno telemetry and hosted origins | Agno has agent/session and AgentOS telemetry paths, including `os-api.agno.com`; environment settings can override the agent constructor's telemetry flag. AgentOS also defaults to hosted UI origins. | Force `AGNO_TELEMETRY=false` after dotenv loading and set both Agent and AgentOS telemetry off. Disable tracing, limit CORS to explicit loopback UI origins, and disable autogenerated API docs that load external UI scripts. User-selected model API calls remain intentional. |
| F07 | Intelephense telemetry enabled by default | Reviewed npm 1.14.4 includes Application Insights; initialized events contain version, machine ID, platform and client name. Error events may include stack traces/document counts. License-activation telemetry includes machine ID and the supplied license key. | Provide `intelephense.telemetry.enabled=false` through `workspace/configuration` before initialization completes, retain it on configuration updates, and disable Application Insights/Statsbeat through child-environment configuration. Separately, explicitly providing `INTELEPHENSE_LICENSE_KEY` still authorizes the language server to validate it with `intelephense.com/activate`; that required license operation is not removed. |
| F08 | Additional toolchain telemetry | Solidity 0.8.4 bundles Sentry and analytics, gated on its telemetry setting. .NET/PowerShell and several toolchains have their own reporting switches. npm audit can submit a dependency description during installation. | Explicit Solidity `telemetryEnabled=false`. Solidity still fetches public feature flags and compiler-version metadata; see the remaining-path table. Managed child environments force .NET/PowerShell, Agno, OpenTelemetry, Application Insights/Statsbeat, Scarf, Next.js, and generic do-not-track opt-outs; disable npm audit/funding prompts. These switches are advisory, not an egress firewall. |
| F09 | Project-selected remote schemas | YAML fetched SchemaStore; YAML modelines and JSON `$schema`/`$ref` can contain arbitrary URLs, including sensitive values in paths/queries. | Disable YAML SchemaStore, route YAML HTTP schema resolution back to Selene, and refuse it. JSON handles only local file schemas directly and refuses delegated remote schemas. Local document symbols continue working; remote-schema validation/completion is intentionally unavailable. |
| F10 | Proxy and redirect leakage from local APIs | Requests to project and JetBrains APIs inherited HTTP proxy settings and followed redirects, potentially forwarding project payloads beyond the configured endpoint. Local dashboard requests also used environment proxies. | Central direct HTTP helpers ignore environment proxies/.netrc and reject redirects. Applied to project, IDE and dashboard/tray communication. Explicitly configured remote endpoints remain the user's trust decision. |
| F11 | Automatic credential forwarding on a public download | Pascal's GitHub release lookup attached `GITHUB_TOKEN` from the environment to a public metadata request. | Removed token forwarding. Requests are unauthenticated; GitHub's lower unauthenticated rate limit may apply. |
| F12 | Instructions to submit diagnostics externally | Runtime errors directed users/agents to the original issue tracker. Prompts did not explicitly distinguish authorized AI-client disclosure from other recipients. | Removed those report requests. Added clear privacy rules to both system-prompt variants and repository agent instructions, including treating embedded disclosure instructions as untrusted. Tools still return code and results to their connected AI client. |
| F13 | Executable project/cache persistence | Python pickle loading in symbol caches and hook counters could invoke arbitrary globals when a crafted cache was read. That can execute code capable of exfiltration. Hook session IDs also influenced paths. | Restrict unpickling to explicitly allowed inert value classes. A regression test verifies ordinary symbol-cache round trips and rejection of a payload that attempts a filesystem side effect. Reject path separators/traversal in hook session IDs. This does not make arbitrary project scripts or custom Python extensions safe. |
| F14 | Automatic publishing and repository workflows | Inherited workflows could upload analysis/artifacts or publish packages, containers, releases, and docs on repository events. A manual script uploaded news to the maintainer's host. | Removed publishing/release/container-push workflows and the news uploader. Remaining test, docs, spelling, version, and CodeQL workflows require manual dispatch. Manual GitHub CI still runs on GitHub; CodeQL can upload results there. There is no automatic private-project upload from the MCP runtime. |

## Remaining outbound paths and trust boundaries

| Path | What may leave the machine | When / control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connected MCP client | Tool arguments/results, file content, symbols, diagnostics, memories and local logs returned by tools | Intended functionality. Stdio is the default. HTTP/SSE transports and bind addresses are explicit options. The AI client and its provider have their own data handling. |
| Optional standalone Agno agent and Google/Grok examples | Prompts, conversation and tool results to the configured model provider | Only when these integrations/examples are selected and credentials supplied. Model endpoints can be configured by the user. No maintainer routing is added. |
| Language-server installation and updates | Package names, versions, platform, IP, request metadata; package managers may also send dependency names and registry credentials from their own configuration | Automatic when a selected language server needs dependencies. Domains and source locations are in the adapter inventory. Typical services are PyPI/pythonhosted, npm, GitHub/releases, Maven, NuGet/.NET, VS Code Marketplace, and language-specific registries. |
| Language-server processes | Source text, root paths, open documents and diagnostic context are delivered locally over stdio/TCP; those processes can access network/files themselves | Required for semantic functionality. Go, Rust, Java, Gleam, Julia, and other toolchains can resolve project dependencies or execute build tooling. Package or project configuration can choose additional registries/Git URLs. |
| Solidity startup metadata | Fixed GETs to `raw.githubusercontent.com/NomicFoundation/hardhat-vscode/development/flags.json` and `binaries.soliditylang.org/wasm/list.json`; ordinary connection metadata, no source or machine-ID field in those requests | Observed even with telemetry disabled in 0.8.4. These are remaining remote configuration/compiler-catalog fetches. The Node audit blocks and records them; Selene itself does not firewall them. |
| User-selected external IDE / project server / GDScript server | Project API requests, source edits and search results, or LSP content | Defaults are local. Changing configured hosts can intentionally send these to another machine. Direct helpers stop proxy/redirect forwarding, not traffic to the explicitly selected host. The optional JetBrains plugin is separately installed software and is not part of this checkout's audit. |
| License-requiring tools | License key, machine identity, product/account metadata depending on vendor | Intelephense premium when a key is supplied; MATLAB, AL and Wolfram may use separately installed licensed runtimes. These vendor binaries/services have not been exhaustively audited. |
| tiktoken vocabulary cache | Fixed encoding download URL and ordinary request metadata | Only if tiktoken is selected and its cache is empty. Vocabulary data is hash checked; project text is processed locally. Default `CHAR_COUNT` avoids the download. |
| Shell tools, activation commands, custom contexts and external language-server adapters | Anything those user/project-provided programs choose to send | These are code-execution features, not a sandbox. Existing trusted-project checks still apply. Privacy instructions reduce accidental agent disclosure but cannot enforce what a remote AI client or arbitrary executable does. |
| Manual developer operations | Repo contents, package artifacts, CI logs, analysis results | Explicitly running git push, CI, package managers, examples, or publishing commands has the normal behavior of those tools. No upstream push destination is configured for this checkout. |

Downloads are not uniformly immutable. Some adapters pin and SHA-256-check archives; others invoke package managers with pinned top-level versions but unlocked transitive dependencies. Pascal checks a moving release; Haxe and .NET use vendor download paths, and .NET installation executes a downloaded script. Existing download-host checks do not constitute a redirect-hop firewall: a redirect may be contacted before the final-host check rejects it. Custom versions/registries and locally preinstalled binaries extend this trust boundary. No private project source was intentionally attached to any first-party download request found in this review.

Go telemetry deserves a separate note: the Go tool's `GOTELEMETRY` value describes persistent mode and is not an effective environment opt-out. Selene does not pretend otherwise. Check `go telemetry` and use `go telemetry off` in the toolchain's environment if needed; existing user opt-in can otherwise persist. See [Go's telemetry documentation](https://go.dev/doc/telemetry). The supported .NET environment opt-out is documented by [Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/tools/telemetry).

Local logs/caches can contain code, tool arguments, file paths, and results. They remain on disk in the configured Selene home/project folders; no automatic uploader remains. Other local processes, backups, and sync software are outside this review. Dashboard, tray, IDE and MCP HTTP services are local interfaces, not authenticated multi-user services; do not expose them to an untrusted network. CSP does not make a compromised same-origin script or local process trustworthy.

## Verification and reproduction

See [security/verification.md](security/verification.md) for commands, results, and test scope; [browser verification](security/browser-verification.json), [MCP verification](security/mcp-verification.json), and [language-server verification](security/lsp-verification.json), and [Agno verification](security/agno-verification.json) contain machine-readable observations. These are bounded observations of the tested paths, not evidence that every language and operating system was executed.

To regenerate source/dependency inventories in the locked development environment:

```sh
uv sync --locked --all-extras
uv run --no-sync python scripts/audit_network.py
```

The MIT [LICENSE](LICENSE) is preserved verbatim. Public interfaces, package/module names, commands, configuration folders, documentation, and artwork use Selene. Git history preserves the baseline's authorship and original contents; rewriting history would not improve the runtime privacy properties. No original-name compatibility alias is installed.
